first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction improve early adoption. This directly addresses the current funnel problems without repeating the retention risk observed with promotional pricing. Verify both related records before committing, then run a controlled experiment focused on qualified activation and downstream revenue quality.

final.rationale: Run a guarded onboarding-shortening experiment, prioritizing self-serve SMB accounts where activation and completion are currently under pressure. Memory_86 shows improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention; memory_31 supports signup simplification for SMBs but includes a 1% retention decline and was not replicated outside that segment. Measure qualified revenue, activation, completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, with retention and qualified-revenue guardrails before expansion.
